verdicts.summary: I could not break the combined rev-parse. Which result is accepted depends on the exit code, so output that has been echoed, contains a newline or is truncated cannot be mistaken for the fast path. When it falls back, it runs the same commands and labels as before.
verdicts.scenario: Tried four cases. (a) Git before 2.31 echoes `--path-format=absolute`: you get 5 lines when HEAD exists or 4 when it is unborn, against the 4 or 3 expected, so it falls back. (b) Only the index path contains a newline, e.g. a linked worktree's gitdir, with an unborn HEAD (exit 1): 4 lines against the 3 expected, so it falls back. It cannot pass as the HEAD-exists case, because the expected count comes from exitCode, not from the line count. (c) Not a repo, or dubious ownership (exit 128): headChecked is false, and resolveGitCommonDir (line 822, no allowNonZeroExit) throws with the old label. (d) CRLF output: `trim()` removes the `\r` and the line count is unchanged. With --verify --quiet, only a HEAD that does not resolve gives exit 1, which matches the old hasHeadCommit rule (any non-zero means no HEAD, line 800). The new call sets allowNonZeroExit, so neither the darwin fsync retry (VcsProcess.ts:282) nor the transient retry (VcsProcess.ts:361-365) can fire on it. That loses nothing: the old resolveGitCommonDir used a non-capture operation and was never retried either.
